_note: Gear v1 weapon catalog (data-driven, same pattern as abilities.json). damageMult joins the hero's damage chain (base x talent x level x timing x WEAPON). reach = MELEE hitbox radius in metres for MELEE jobs (knight) — overrides PlayerAttackController's fixed AttackRange (3.2) when >0; a heavier/longer blade outreaches a lighter one. Ranged jobs (mage/ranger) attack via AbilityDef.Range and leave reach 0 (unset) so their range is unchanged. req starts level-gated; add dex/arcane/might keys later. icon = emoji placeholder until real art ships (swap the field, zero code change). PRICING (buyWood/buyFood/buyIron/buyCrystals): tiered by rarity (common floor -> legendary sink, ~2.5x/tier); CRYSTALS gate rare+ (the aether/crystal arc); resource mix reflects the weapon's nature (knight=iron blade, ranger=wood bow, mage=wood staff + crystal head). Lean economy by design.

weapons.name: Oakheart Staff
weapons.flavor: Shaped from a fallen oak at the forest's edge, before the Heartwood guild ever thought to grow such things with intention.

weapons.name: Arcane Scepter
weapons.flavor: Cut in the Bright Centuries, when an Elarion-forged head still drank the Heart's light without dimming.

weapons.name: Voidcaller Staff
weapons.flavor: A late-age masterwork. Pressed to the ear in a quiet room, the crystal is said to hum the old singing note.

weapons.name: Squire's Blade
weapons.flavor: Plain iron, no mark, no history — the sword they give you before you have earned one.

weapons.name: Squire's Heater
weapons.flavor: A plain iron-banded heater — the first thing a squire is taught to hold.

weapons.name: Iron Longsword
weapons.flavor: Not beautiful, not storied — just steel that has not failed anyone yet.

weapons.name: Oathkeeper
weapons.flavor: Such blades sealed the highest bonds — given at sworn-knightings, written into wills above land.

weapons.name: Dawnbreaker
weapons.flavor: Kin to the lost Dawnedge, gifted to a southern queen at her crowning. To hold one was to be someone.

weapons.name: Hunter's Shortbow
weapons.flavor: Field-strung and field-forgotten; the kind of bow found in a dead man's pack with no name on it.

weapons.name: Field Arrows
weapons.flavor: Straight ash, grey goose fletching, no cleverness at all. What every quiver holds before it holds anything better.

weapons.name: Emberhead
weapons.flavor: A pitch-soaked head that takes light off the draw. The wound keeps burning after the arrow is pulled.

weapons.name: Venomtip
weapons.flavor: Drawn from the green lanes and left to dry on the head. Two in the same target is twice the walk to the ground.

weapons.name: Rimeshot
weapons.flavor: A crystal head cut cold and kept cold. What it strikes forgets how to hurry.

weapons.name: Acolyte's Mace
weapons.flavor: A simple iron head on a turned handle — the first thing an acolyte raises in blessing, the last thing some enemies saw.

weapons.name: Emberbrand, the Rekindled
weapons.saga: Borin reforged the snapped hilt with the Threefold Fold; Wren's Last Pressing let the steel drink aether without shattering. A combo finisher releases the stored aether as a shock.

weapons.name: Heartwood Longbow
weapons.saga: Pell's living-wood limbs, given by the Tree rather than taken. Charged shots pierce and 'remember' the last struck foe.

weapons.name: Aetherstaff
weapons.saga: A quench-bonded crystal head set in Heartwood — Wren and Pell's craft as one. Spells cost less the closer you fight.

weapons.name: The Hallowed Censer
weapons.saga: Halvard's Oathweld bound to Pell's Heartwood. Its heals also seed a small ward on the Heart and the village's structures.

weapons.name: Reaver's Hatchet
weapons.flavor: Small enough to throw, heavy enough to mean it — the hatchet that ended arguments before they became sieges.

weapons.name: Bramblefang
weapons.flavor: A fast Heartwood dirk; its bite is said to bleed deep.

weapons.name: Wardstone Maul
weapons.flavor: Emberhand maul; a ground-slam stuns and throws sparks.

weapons.name: Oakband Heater
weapons.flavor: Oak-banded and unadorned — the kind of shield that has stopped arrows and never been thanked for it.

weapons.name: Emberglass Staff
weapons.flavor: Emberglass is what happens when a furnace cracks and someone decides to sell the pieces anyway.

weapons.name: Tideglass Staff
weapons.flavor: Tideglass came in on trader ships from the coast — pale blue, cold to the touch, and never quite at home this far inland.

weapons.name: Sparkwood Staff
weapons.flavor: A Last-Pressing crystal head set in sparkwood; it drinks the Heart's light.

weapons.name: Heartglass Rod
weapons.flavor: A rod, not a staff — less reach, less ceremony, and quicker to draw in a room with a low ceiling.

weapons.name: Wardens' Edge
weapons.flavor: The edge they trained wardens on; plain enough that losing one was not a tragedy.

weapons.name: Footman's Cut
weapons.flavor: A footman's blade — weighted for a full day's march and a hard ten minutes at the end of it.
